tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description starts with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review'), focuses on user intent (bill being high, cost per team, idle Provisioned Throughput, quota headroom, etc.) rather than internal mechanics, and aggressively lists many explicit trigger contexts including implicit phrasings a user might use without naming the domain. It also explicitly excludes a scope ('Not for outages happening now'). While dense, it stays as a single coherent paragraph appropriate for the breadth of triggers it needs to cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review, for example why the bill is high or suspiciously low... Not for outages happening now (use llmops-incident-triage).

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and almost entirely domain-specific — AWS Bedrock API quirks, metric names, billing nuances, check-ids, and specific procedures. There is no generic explanation of concepts the agent already knows (no 'what is cost explorer' type filler).
tests.evidence: Group, don't filter: product-attribute filters and `--dimension-key` are rejected.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps detailed tables (check families, router) short and summary-level, pointing to references/ files for full detection rules, remediations and citations rather than embedding large reference blocks inline.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All seven references/ files are linked via markdown links in the body: api-quirks.md, checks-model-invocation.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, collection-reference.md, cost-analysis.md, metrics-and-logs.md, quota-codes.md.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific trigger condition or step, e.g. load collection-reference with any row, cost-analysis before any LLM-COST/PT finding, checks-model-invocation before LLM-INV-002/007.
tests.evidence: Load when the step says so: [cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) (Steps 3–5, before any LLM-COST or LLM-PT finding); [checks-model-invocation.md](references/checks-model-invocation.md) (before LLM-INV-002/007);

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only rules, labeling dollar figures, quota lookup, PT resize prohibition) are given exact prescriptive steps, while sections like check severity decisions ('decide 003/004 from the invocation pattern and the stated workload') leave room for judgment, showing calibrated specificity.
tests.evidence: PT can't be resized in place (`UpdateProvisionedModelThroughput` changes only the name or model): give the LLM-PT-001 remediation, never an update command.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The router table gives a clear default first read for each scenario rather than listing multiple equal tool options, and rate-lookup order designates a clear primary source with fallbacks.
tests.evidence: **Rates**, in order: the user (say so); `pricing:GetProducts` (us-east-1, one call per model...); or the [pricing page]... read with `verify_aws_claim`.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The procedure teaches a generalizable method (scope → tokens → cost model → coverage check → checks → PT → headroom → alarms → assemble) applicable to any Bedrock cost review, not a one-off declaration for a specific account/model.
tests.evidence: Step 1: **Scope:** region(s), window, models and profiles; state the defaults chosen (current region, trailing window).

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive 'Common wrong answers' section plus 'Error Handling' detailing non-obvious API behaviors and misconceptions, functioning as a gotchas section.
tests.evidence: **"A `us.` profile bills as us-east-1."** It is a geographic routing scope; billing follows the source region (api-quirks §14, LLM-COST-005).

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured cost/capacity report and provides a dedicated template asset for it.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the actual report template is stored in assets/ and only referenced.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The sole asset file capacity-cost-report-template.md is linked in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies it is used 'only for a full report', giving a clear condition for when to load it.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path assets/capacity-cost-report-template.md with no absolute path or traversal.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow 'Procedure — Capacity & Cost Review' is presented as a checkbox checklist with Step N format, and sub-bullets under each step elaborate without introducing a conflicting numbering scheme.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' checklist instructing the agent to check its own output for errors (labels, windows, divergence, check-ids) before presenting.
tests.evidence:
A confidently wrong cost number is worse than a slow one. If an item can't be met, say so.
- [ ] Every top rule and "Guardrails — details" holds; no 12-digit number.
